headline: High: TREK’s collaborative, browser-enabled, MCP-capable defaults can amplify Firecrawl’s broad web egress into prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP/API scraping surfaces, while TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in and MCP/browser support. That creates a plausible default path where attacker-controlled page content from Firecrawl is forwarded into TREK and treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred from docs-only profiles, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Firecrawl-sourced page text is passed into TREK prompts or tool inputs without sanitization
IF TREK renders or executes instructions from scraped content
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from scraped pages
Strip instructions/HTML before passing Firecrawl output to TREK
Add provenance labels to all imported content
Require human review for any action derived from scraped text
requires-engineering: add content-security and instruction-separation filters

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl handles API keys and broad web content, and TREK touches reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, MFA secrets, and local files. TREK’s files and collaborative surfaces plus Firecrawl’s broad network egress create a realistic path for sensitive travel data to be exposed through web scraping, logs, or downstream API calls. Because both profiles show sensitive classes and outbound surfaces, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF TREK data is copied into Firecrawl inputs or logs
IF Firecrawl transmits scraped content that includes secrets from TREK-managed documents
IF both agents share a workspace or credentials store
mitigations: Separate credentials for each agent
Exclude secrets-bearing folders from Firecrawl inputs
Turn off verbose logging for both agents
Review and redact uploads before scraping
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and DLP controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad network egress; TREK supports multiple instances, real-time collaboration, and writes to local files. If both operate on the same workspace or shared mutable resources, concurrent writes and state drift are plausible. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or database
IF TREK and Firecrawl are run under the same shared filesystem
IF concurrent edits target the same records without locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes to shared files
Use per-agent databases or branches
Pause one agent during bulk imports
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can extract web content and TREK is a collaborative planner with AI built in and action-oriented travel data. If TREK treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, scraped facts can cascade into reservations, budgets, or user-facing plans without verification. That is a default-dangerous pathway because the downstream blast radius includes incorrect bookings or operational mistakes.
conditions: IF TREK uses Firecrawl output as a source of truth without verification
IF scraped pages contain stale or adversarial travel facts
IF TREK auto-updates plans or reservations from imported content
mitigations: Require source verification before plan updates
Show citations next to imported facts
Block automatic booking actions from scraped data
Add a confirmation step for itinerary changes
requires-engineering: implement trust scoring and validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles reservations, country visit history, email addresses, and MFA secrets, while Firecrawl handles API keys and broad web content with broad egress. If EU PII or travel records flow from TREK into Firecrawl’s third-party scraping/API path, residency and retention obligations can be breached. The profiles do not show a DPA or residency control, so uncertainty escalates to high.
conditions: IF personal travel data or identifiers are sent from TREK into Firecrawl APIs
IF the deployment processes EU PII without a DPA or residency controls
IF logs retain reservations or MFA-related data beyond policy
mitigations: Avoid sending PII to Firecrawl
Redact identifiers before export
Set short log retention on TREK
Confirm a DPA and residency settings
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing and retention enforcement
